Now Abraham was old, advanced in years, and Yahweh had blessed Abraham in everything.
And Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his household, who governed all that he had, "Please put your hand under my thigh,
and I will make you swear by Yahweh, the God of the heavens and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I am living,
but you will go to my land and to my relatives and take a wife for my son, for Isaac."
And the servant said to him, "Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land. Should I really take your son back to the land that you came out of?"
And Abraham said to him, "Be careful that you do not take my son back there.

Yahweh, the God of the heavens, who took me from my father's house and from the land of my birth, and who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, 'To your offspring I will give this land,' he will send his angel before you, and you will take a wife for my son from there.
But if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you will be clear of this oath of mine. Only my son you must not take back there."
And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.
And the servant took ten camels from his master's camels and went, with all the good things of his master in his hand. And he rose and went to Aram-Naharaim, to the city of Nahor.
And he made the camels kneel outside the city by the well of water at evening time, at the time when the women who draw water come out.
And he said, "Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, please make it happen before me today, and show faithful love to my master Abraham.
Look, I am standing by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

And may it be that the young woman to whom I say, 'Please tilt your jar, so that I may drink,' and who says, 'Drink, and I will water your camels too'—she is the one you have decided on for your servant, for Isaac. And by her I will know that you have shown faithful love to my master."
And before he had finished speaking, look, Rebekah was coming out, who had been born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and her jar was on her shoulder.
Now the young woman was very beautiful in appearance, a virgin, and no man had been intimate with her. And she went down to the spring and filled her jar and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her and said, "Please let me sip a little water from your jar."
And she said, "Drink, my lord," and she hurried and let down her jar onto her hand and gave him a drink.
And when she had finished giving him a drink, she said, "For your camels too I will draw, until they have finished drinking."
And she hurried and emptied her jar into the trough and ran again to the well to draw, and she drew for all his camels.
And the man was gazing at her [alt: was astonished at her], keeping silent, to know whether Yahweh had made his way succeed or not.
And when the camels had finished drinking, the man took a gold ring, a beka in weight, and two bracelets for her arms, ten shekels of gold in weight.
And he said, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there a place at your father's house for us to spend the night?"
And she said to him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor."
And she said to him, "We have plenty of both straw and fodder, and also a place to spend the night."
And the man bowed his head and bowed down to Yahweh.

And he said, "Blessed is Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who has not abandoned his faithful love and his truth toward my master. As for me, Yahweh has led me on the way to the house of my master's brothers."
And the young woman ran and told her mother's household about these things.
Now Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban. And Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.

And when he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister's arms, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, "This is how the man spoke to me," he came to the man, and look, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
And he said, "Come in, blessed of Yahweh. Why are you standing outside, when I have cleared the house, and a place for the camels?"
And the man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels and gave straw and fodder to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
And food was set before him to eat, but he said, "I will not eat until I have spoken my words." And he said, "Speak."
And he said, "I am Abraham's servant.
And Yahweh has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great. And he has given him flocks and cattle and silver and gold and male slaves and female slaves and camels and donkeys.
And Sarah, my master's wife, bore a son to my master after she had grown old, and he has given him all that he has.
And my master made me swear, saying, 'You must not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I am living.
Rather, you are to go to my father's house and to my family and take a wife for my son.'
And I said to my master, 'Perhaps the woman will not follow me.'
And he said to me, 'Yahweh, before whom I have walked, will send his angel with you and make your way succeed, and you will take a wife for my son from my family and from my father's house.
Then you will be clear of my curse, when you come to my family; and if they do not give one to you, you will be clear of my curse.'
And I came today to the spring and said, 'Yahweh, God of my master Abraham, please, if you are going to make my way succeed, the way on which I am going,
look, I am standing by the spring of water. And may it be that the girl who comes out to draw, to whom I say, "Please give me a little water to drink from your jar,"
and who says to me, "Drink, you too, and I will also draw for your camels"—she is the woman whom Yahweh has decided on for my master's son.'
Before I had finished speaking to my heart, look, Rebekah was coming out with her jar on her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew. And I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'
And she hurried and let down her jar from her shoulder and said, 'Drink, and I will water your camels too.' And I drank, and she watered the camels too.
And I asked her and said, 'Whose daughter are you?' And she said, 'The daughter of Bethuel the son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.' And I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
And I bowed my head and bowed down to Yahweh, and I blessed Yahweh, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on a true way to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.
And now, if you are going to show loyalty and truth to my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left."
And Laban and Bethuel answered and said, "From Yahweh the matter has come; we cannot speak to you bad or good.
Look, Rebekah is before you. Take her and go, and let her be a wife to your master's son, as Yahweh has spoken."
And when Abraham's servant heard their words, he bowed down to the ground to Yahweh.
And the servant brought out articles of silver and articles of gold, and garments, and gave them to Rebekah, and he gave precious things to her brother and to her mother.
And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and they spent the night. And they rose in the morning, and he said, "Send me on my way to my master."
And her brother and her mother said, "Let the young woman stay with us a few days, or ten [alt: a year, or ten months]; afterward she may go."
And he said to them, "Do not delay me, when Yahweh has made my way succeed. Send me on my way, so that I may go to my master."
And they said, "Let us call the young woman and ask her herself."
And they called Rebekah and said to her, "Will you go with this man?" And she said, "I will go."
And they sent Rebekah their sister on her way, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant and his men.
And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, may you become thousands of ten thousands, and may your offspring take possession of the gate of those who hate them."
And Rebekah rose, and her young women, and they rode on the camels and followed the man. And the servant took Rebekah and went.
Now Isaac had come from going to Beer-Lahai-Roi, and he was living in the land of the Negev.
And Isaac went out to meditate [alt: to walk about] in the field toward evening, and he lifted his eyes and saw, and look, camels were coming.
And Rebekah lifted her eyes and saw Isaac, and she dropped down from the camel.
And she said to the servant, "Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?" And the servant said, "He is my master." And she took her veil and covered herself.
And the servant recounted to Isaac all the things that he had done.
And Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, and he took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. And Isaac was comforted after his mother.
